### Security-sensitive behavior

The SDK structured I/O path still accepts hook-rewritten input without the
same rule revalidation used by the main tool path:

| Path | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `reconstructed/v2.1.112/src/cli/structuredIO.ts:937` | Computes `finalInput = decision.updatedInput || input`. |
| `reconstructed/v2.1.112/src/cli/structuredIO.ts:939` | Comment notes the missing v112 ask-rule check. |
| `reconstructed/v2.1.112/src/cli/structuredIO.ts:955` | Returns `behavior: 'allow'` without rule revalidation. |
| `reconstructed/v2.1.112/src/services/tools/toolHooks.ts:373` | Main tool path calls `checkRuleBasedPermissions(...)` before accepting hook approval. |

This is a policy bypass risk for SDK/structured I/O reconstruction quality,
not just a typecheck issue.

## Current Verdict

`reconstructed/v2.1.112` improved substantially after wave 17 because the
React Compiler cache artifact class is closed. It is still not audit-grade
source: the internal module graph does not resolve, bridge and permission
paths contain hard behavior-changing placeholders, and many embedded source
maps remain.

Do not use `reconstructed/v2.1.112` as a source of truth for patch rationale
until the open gates above are closed. It is acceptable as a work-in-progress
lift corpus for targeted recovery.
